subject.title: fix(acp): exit help and EOF cleanly

question: Should ACP intentionally reject a client after more than 1 MiB of input arrives before Gateway readiness, or must startup preserve the prior backpressure/no-drop behavior for larger queued input?
rationale: The branch introduces a concrete new transport limit while solving EOF detection; source-level review alone cannot determine whether that limit is compatible with ACP client expectations.

options.title: Define and prove the bounded limit
options.body: Keep the 1 MiB cap only with an explicit expected failure mode and focused boundary coverage showing clients receive a clear, safe outcome.

options.title: Preserve larger queued input
options.body: Redesign the startup monitor so EOF detection does not impose a new fixed pre-Gateway payload limit on valid ACP clients.

options.title: Pause for ACP contract review
options.body: Hold the change until the ACP owner confirms the intended startup buffering and backpressure contract.

recommendation.title: Define and prove the bounded limit
recommendation.body: Keep the 1 MiB cap only with an explicit expected failure mode and focused boundary coverage showing clients receive a clear, safe outcome.

likelyOwner.reason: The current ACP change is assigned to steipete, making them the best available routing point for the startup-stream contract decision.
